:::{#thm-chebyshev-sample-mean}
#### Chebyshev's inequality for a sample average

Let $\dsn{X}$ be [IID](independence.qmd#def-iid) random variables
with mean $\mean$ and finite variance $\varpar > 0$,
and let $\bar X_n \eqdef \frac{1}{n}\sumin X_i$.
Then for every $\epsilon > 0$:

$$
\Prf{\abs{\bar X_n - \mean} \ge \epsilon} \le \frac{\varpar}{n\epsilon^2}
$$

:::

::: proof

This is the solution to @exr-chebyshev-sample-size (a).
Let $S_n \eqdef \sumin X_i$.
By @cor-sum-iid-moments, $\Var{S_n} = n\varpar$,
so $\bar X_n = S_n/n$ has mean $\mean$ and variance $\varpar/n$
(a constant factor $c$ scales a variance by $c^2$).
Apply @thm-chebyshev to $\bar X_n$ with $k\sdpar/\sqrt{n} = \epsilon$,
that is, $k = \epsilon\sqrt{n}/\sdpar$, so $1/k^2 = \varpar/(n\epsilon^2)$.

:::
